design: Two-player zero-sum loop. Player A = the trading policy pi (per-asset daily weight vector; the "controller"). Player B = a market generator G that emits paths inside a plausibility set U and is rewarded by pi's loss: (i) RARL/Spooner-style, where G controls bounded drift/vol/correlation knobs on real or Bella paths step by step; (ii) Wasserstein-DRO, where U = {P : W_2(P, P_n) <= delta} around the empirical panel; (iii) PAIRED-style regret (TASK_110 as written: G = Bella flow-matching conditioned on regime, reward = hindsight-oracle regret); (iv) domain randomisation over Bella regimes (the degenerate one-player case). pi is trained on the min over U (or its CVaR); the learned G is then offered to Monte Carlo search as the leaf/rollout distribution ("patterns that serve Monte Carlo"). Objective in all variants: max_pi min_{P in U} E_P[U(net PnL at fee16/slip5)].
what_the_loop_learns: Two objects. (1) G_adv = argmin_{P in U} E_P[utility(pi)] — a distribution over paths concentrated on pi's WORST cases. Its information is about the POLICY (where pi is fragile), not about the market: a generator fitted to the same OHLC panel cannot hold more conditional-mean information than a forecaster fitted to that panel; its drift channel is a lower-sample-efficiency forecaster. (2) The robust pi* = the minimax fixed point. Closed form for the Wasserstein ball (Blanchet-Chen-Zhou, Prop. 1, read in full): min_{P in U_delta} E_P[phi^T R] = mu_hat^T phi - sqrt(delta)*||phi||_p — the adversary shaves sqrt(delta)*||phi|| off the drift IN THE DIRECTION OF THE POSITION, and Theorem 1 turns the whole problem into variance minimisation plus a norm penalty. By Holder, mu_hat^T phi <= ||mu_hat||_q ||phi||_p, so the robust worst-case mean of ANY book is <= 0 whenever sqrt(delta) >= ||mu_hat||_q; the robust book is nonzero only in directions where the estimated drift exceeds the radius PLUS costs — i.e. exactly a t-statistic gate on a forecast. Paper's own words (§3.1): "If delta is too large ... the resulting optimal portfolios will tend to be just equal allocations." RARL analogue, Spooner-Savani 2020 Thm 1 (full read): the drift adversary plays b* = b_low when inventory H > 0 and b_high when H < 0, so the equilibrium market maker holds ~zero inventory (terminal inventory -0.05 +/- 1.94 under the STRATEGIC adversary vs 0.56 +/- 7.55 without) and lives off spread capture. A daily directional trader has no spread income; its "zero inventory" is FLAT. So the loop learns, beyond a direct estimator: nothing about expected return; a stress distribution over the policy's failure paths; and a shrinkage rule that is algebraically a confidence-bound filter on whatever forecast the ambiguity set failed to erase. In the repo's own terms it FORMALISES 887's attractor rather than escaping it.
worth_if_ic_is_zero: If daily conditional-mean IC ~ 0, mu_hat is sampling noise, any data-driven radius (delta = O(1/n), RWPI) covers it, and pi* is flat for a cost-charged long-short book or 1/N for a long-only constraint — both already measured: HOLD/flat is 887 (A 99.0% hold, return -2.86%; forcing action loses monotonically, -9.1% / -13.8%, at fee 0 — LEDGER row 887 line 97) and 812 (100% HOLD OOS, `lore/notes_2026-06-26.md:104-117`); the 1/N constant mix is measured PIT gross -0.40 FULL / -2.54 BEAR22 (`lore/fable_tactics_panel_2026-09-04.md:80`, `trader/backtest.py:225-227`). Alpha value of the loop = 0. Residual value = (a) a machine-checkable certificate "no pi in class Pi has positive worst-case EV over U" — the record already has this empirically six ways; (b) a regime-stress generator for R4 (`docs/pathway.md:84-85`); (c) a risk-sizing/shrinkage rule. If U is made SMALL enough to leave a non-flat pi*, the loop degenerates to training on generator samples = the 758 data-augmentation arm, measured paired -16.54pp then re-characterised NULL +0.13pp (`docs/findings/encoder_bella_class_closed.md:9-12, :22`).
measured_failure_mode_and_escape: Must escape 887/collapse-confirm: the policy abstains because its own actions have negative EV, adaptively, at zero cost (LEDGER line 97; pre-figured by 812 on the scalar stack, `docs/pathfinder_audit_2026-08-19.md:50`). Mechanically, minimax makes that abstention a THEOREM instead of an empirical fixed point: any plausibility set containing a zero-drift or drift-reflected measure gives every position worst-case EV <= -cost(turnover), minimised at flat. The only mechanical escape is to constrain U so that for some phi, min_{P in U} E_P[phi^T R] > cost(phi) — i.e. to assert a directional prior with a confidence radius. That constraint IS a forecast with a t-stat, which is the memo's §4 IC instrument (G-A: IC >= 0.02, NW t >= 3, `lore/fable_direction_memo_2026-09-03.md:306-308`). There is no escape inside the loop; the escape is the instrument outside it. Second measured mode the PAIRED variant must escape and cannot: regret against a hindsight oracle saturates. `diff_teacher/adversarial_training.py:355` computes regret = (optimal - actual)/|optimal| with `optimal_solver.py:2-4` a perfect-foresight oracle; the real-panel oracle ceiling is +29.7 net@21 / per-asset gross alpha +75.5 (LEDGER 830/E0-REAL line 46), so against a ~HOLD policy regret ≡ 1 on every path — the generator's objective is flat in path structure and only the realism/diversity terms carry signal (and the trainer never implemented a gradient step anyway: `adversarial_training.py:410-411` "track metrics only ... TODO: Implement proper gradient-based update"). PAIRED's own finding (Dennis 2020): a minimax adversary produces unsolvable environments; regret needs a competent antagonist, not an oracle. Third: 892's anti-edge lives in maintenance re-trims (LEDGER line 102) — a robust loop WOULD suppress re-trims, but that is cost reduction (tactics panel row 2), not expectation.

bear_positive_without_forecast.argument: BEAR-positive requires E[PnL | bear] > 0. Under a plausibility set symmetric in drift (or merely containing a zero-drift member), the robust book is flat, whose bear PnL is 0 minus nothing — not positive. Under a long-only constraint the robust limit is equal allocation (Blanchet §3.1), which carries beta and is measured negative in every bear (EW 1/N PIT gross -2.54 BEAR22; the only bear-positive behaviour in the record is the trend book's SHORT leg, BEAR22 +1.095 vs long-flat -2.471, LEDGER 898 line 103 — a forecast). Robustness against a drift adversary strictly REMOVES directional exposure; it cannot manufacture the short-in-bear tilt. The Spooner-Savani result is the clean demonstration: Sharpe 5.57 -> 9.78 came from terminal-wealth std 12.0 -> 6.7 while the MEAN FELL 67.0 -> 65.1 — robustness bought variance, not expectation, and their agent had spread income to keep the mean positive. A daily spot book has no such exogenous income. Conditional only in the trivial sense: if U excludes bear-adverse drift, U encodes a bear forecast.

literature.ref: Spooner & Savani 2020, 'Robust Market Making via Adversarial Reinforcement Learning', IJCAI-20 pp. 4590-4596 (arXiv 2003.01820)
literature.claim: Zero-sum game: MM vs adversary controlling drift b in [-5,5], arrival A in [105,175], decay k in [1.125,1.875] of an Avellaneda-Stoikov mid-price Z_{n+1}=Z_n+b dt+sigma W. Single-stage NE (Thm 1): adversary sets drift AGAINST inventory (b_low if H>0, b_high if H<0); MM spread delta = 1/k +/- b. Robust MM converges to ~zero inventory and earns from spread; robustness = variance reduction. Authors note inventory penalties yield 'strategies that try to avoid trading at all, a frequent problem in this domain'.
literature.numbers: RN MM trained vs FIXED: terminal wealth 67.0+/-12.0, Sharpe 5.57, terminal inventory 0.56+/-7.55. Trained vs STRATEGIC (b,A,k): 65.1+/-6.7, Sharpe 9.78, inventory -0.05+/-1.94; drift-only adversary 9.51 (+0.27 from full). FIXED-trained MMs tested under RANDOM adversary: +98.1% variance; RANDOM-trained +86.0%. Evaluated over 1e5 episodes, no transaction costs beyond spread model.

literature.ref: Blanchet, Chen & Zhou 2022 (arXiv 1802.04885 v1, 2018), 'Distributionally Robust Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection with Wasserstein Distances', Management Science 68(9)
literature.claim: Prop. 1: min_{P: W(P,P_n)<=delta} E_P[phi^T R] = E_{P_n}[phi^T R] - sqrt(delta)||phi||_p. Thm 1: DRO mean-variance == min_phi (sqrt(phi^T Var_{P_n} phi) + sqrt(delta)||phi||_p)^2 — robustness is exactly a norm penalty shrinking positions; §3.1: too-large delta -> equal allocations; delta should be O(1/n), chosen by RWPI at a confidence level (95%).
literature.numbers: Worst-case drift shave = sqrt(delta)*||phi||_p per unit; robust book nonzero only where mu_hat^T phi > sqrt(delta)||phi||_p (a t-stat gate). v1 read contains no empirical Sharpe table (theory + proofs, 20 pp).

literature.ref: Pinto, Davidson, Sukthankar & Gupta 2017, 'Robust Adversarial Reinforcement Learning', ICML 70:2817-2826
literature.claim: Minimax zero-sum training against a destabilising adversary applying disturbance forces; improves stability and train/test robustness; outperforms baseline even without adversary on MuJoCo tasks. Key disanalogy: the adversary perturbs dynamics the agent CONTROLS; in a market the price is exogenous and only inventory is controlled.

kill_experiment.design: Ambiguity-radius sweep on the tactic library (formalises the minimax argument on the real PIT panel without training anything). Panel: PIT 273-asset true UTC daily panel 2024-01 -> 2026-06 via trader/data.py:192. Policy class Pi: the tactics panel's K~8 position matrices (flat; 819 trend; long-flat trend; EW constant mix; beta-hedged mix; vol-targeted trend; 7d and 21d cross-sectional reversal L/S) x a sizing scalar s in {0, .25, .5, 1} (the 'inventory' the robust solver can shrink). Nested plausibility sets: U0 = {real panel}; U1 = U0 + circular block bootstrap of dates (block 21, M=200); U2 = U1 + blockwise time-reversal; U3 = U2 + global reflection of the market-residual return component (r_resid -> -r_resid for all assets together, covariance preserved; includes the zero-drift measure by symmetry); U4 (optional GPU arm) = Bella regime-conditioned daily paths. Robust selector per U_r: pi* = argmax over Pi of the 10th-percentile net@21 Sharpe over U_r (also record the pure min). Then realise every selected pi* on the unseen 2026H1 slice. Pre-register: SPEC <= 1 page, sha256 recorded, cell grid fixed.
kill_experiment.instrument: Unmodified trader.backtest.cell_metrics (trader/backtest.py:231) with _block_bootstrap_sharpe_ci (trader/backtest.py:157), seed 819, n_boot 2000, tiers 8/21, PIT universe via trader/cli.py build_pit_universe; simple AND log portfolio returns both reported (tactics panel correction 2); exposure and turnover printed beside every Sharpe (898 confound rule).
kill_experiment.pass_fail: P1 (loop formalises no-edge): for U3 the robust selector picks flat or s=0 in each of 2024, 2025, 2026H1. P1 holding => any minimax loop whose plausibility set admits drift reflection outputs flat by construction; GPU version killed. P2 (robustness creates Sharpe): some intermediate radius (U1 or U2) selects a non-flat tactic whose realised UNSEEN 2026H1 net@21 beats BOTH the nominal U0 choice and flat by more than the bootstrap CI half-width, AND that tactic is positive in 2024 and 2025. P2 PASS does not license the loop — it says the plausibility set encodes a usable prior, which is handed to the IC instrument (G-A) to name the forecast. P1 holds and P2 fails => family closed for alpha; only the honest uses remain. Expected outcome: P1 holds, P2 fails.
kill_experiment.cost: CPU minutes to ~1 hour; <=1 day implementer time; zero GPU (optional U4 arm ~1 GPU-hour if checkpoints/diff_teacher loads on daily bars). Kill date 7 days from SPEC commit.

honest_odds: P(an adversarial/minimax self-play loop is the SOURCE of a book clearing the goalposts) ≈ 0-1%: the fixed point is flat unless the plausibility set carries a forecast, and the record already sits at that fixed point (887, 812). P(kill experiment P2 PASS, i.e. some finite radius selects a tactic that beats nominal and flat on unseen 2026H1) ≈ 5-10%, and a PASS is a forecast finding routed to the IC instrument, not a loop finding. P(the honest uses — R4 stress gate, DRO shrinkage sizing, surrogate null family — add measurable value to a book that has already passed G-A/G-B) ≈ 60-70%, at +0 expected Sharpe and some variance/drawdown reduction. Recommendation: do not build the loop; run the CPU kill experiment only if the operator wants the closure on record; put the 64 GB cards on nothing in this family until the IC ceiling is measured.
open_doubts: Blanchet-Chen-Zhou is a one-period static result; they leave the dynamic DRO Markowitz open. A path-dependent adversary interacting with proportional-cost no-trade bands could in principle produce a non-flat robust policy (wider bands, not new expectation) — argued by analogy, not proven here.

Second-moment predictability (vol clustering, correlation regimes) is real and a generator can carry it; a robust controller exploiting it is a sizing/cost lever (tactics panel row 4, 1-2%), not expected return — but the sizing gain on a passing forecast has never been measured in this repo.
Bella's fidelity on daily bars is unmeasured (trained on 400-step minute windows); the optional U4 arm may fail for that reason alone, which would be a Bella finding, not a loop finding.

Spooner-Savani's extended arXiv version (three-parameter adversary proofs) and the 2026 Bayesian-robust paper body were not read; statements about their cost handling and baselines are abstract-level.

The reflection surrogate (U3) must flip the residual component globally to preserve covariance; per-asset independent flips would alter correlation signs and make the null too strong — a pre-registration detail, flagged.

If the operator's 'whisper' meant Bella as MCTS leaf rollouts (TASK_778) rather than adversarial training, the same information argument applies (no drift beyond a forecaster; 831x/C locates search value in true lookahead), but 778 has genuinely never been run.
